incident-bot: [ALERT] P1 detected: KV cache paging + eviction spike on orb-uk-3. Eviction rate ~11x baseline, paging ops increased ~6x, tail token latency >2.5x. Auto-mitigation attempted (continuous-batch backpressure) and failed to reduce paging.

maria nguyen: ACKing, jumping in. tagging @leo @aj. any quick indicators for scope? :eyes:

leo park: looking at ingest heatmap — two hot prefixes causing KV thrash, continuous batching cadence shows long in-flight windows (~70ms) that line up with huge KV lookups. stack traces show partial flushes getting queued. customer error rate up ~0.2% in last 12m.

aj singh: initial hunch: recent rollout of `kv.batch_window_ms=70` and `continuous_batch.enabled=true` likely amplified prefetch -> eviction loop. those small hot prefixes keep getting re-requested, filling cache and triggering paging.

emily chen: on it. I'm preparing a quick revert/hotpatch to reduce window and add a defensive partial-flush guard (skip if inflight > X). will push as a config override if safe.

maria nguyen: we need to quantify customer impact before broad changes. @carla can you pull SLO hit / user-facing metrics?

carla reyes: pulling evals — so far 3.1% of production requests in the last 30m experienced latency >2s, error spikes mostly 502 from our gateway when KV lookups time out. Affected surfaces: conversational chat beta and similarity-search for a handful of large tenants. No full customer outages reported yet.

leo park: adding quick log snippet from node kv-12:
```
[2026-02-14T11:09:23Z] eviction_rate=1245/s, paging_ops=634/s, batch_window_ms=70, inflight_tokens=12
[2026-02-14T11:09:24Z] partial_flush_attempt=1, flush_queued=true
[2026-02-14T11:09:25Z] kernel_latency_ms=312
```

aj singh: plan proposal — two-step mitigation:
1) immediate: disable continuous batching for the kv-cache service (cheap toggle) to stop amplification.
2) short-term: revert `kv.batch_window_ms` to 20ms and deploy a guard to ignore partial flushes when eviction_rate > threshold.
3) monitor for paging reduction, then can re-enable with stricter per-prefix throttles.

emily chen: applying step 1 now as a config override to prod (canary 5% -> 20% -> 60% if green). command:
```
redwood-cli config apply --env prod --service kv-cache --set continuous_batch.enabled=false --canary 5
```

ops-bot: Deploy started: config-override/kv-cache/continuous-batch-toggle by emily. Canary 5% -> 20% in 3m windows.

emily chen: canary 5% applied. watching telemetry.

maria nguyen: add a short status note for customers ops team. @carla can you draft an initial blurb if we see improvement?

carla reyes: drafted: "We observed elevated latency and paging in our KV cache impacting a subset of customers' similarity and chat requests. We're rolling a configuration hotfix to reduce batching amplification and have temporarily disabled continuous batching while we stabilize. We're monitoring and will share updates." want me to send to accounts?

leo park: metrics update after 8m — eviction_rate down to ~1.4x baseline, paging_ops down ~55% vs peak, tail latency trending down toward baseline. looks promising.

ops-bot: Canary rollout success: 5% -> 20% -> 60% completed. No rollout failures.

emily chen: moving to step 2 now: revert `kv.batch_window_ms` from 70 -> 20 in prod and push partial-flush guard. will do quick 10% canary.
```
redwood-cli config apply --env prod --service kv-cache --set kv.batch_window_ms=20 --set kv.partial_flush_guard=true --canary 10
```

aj singh: heads-up: partial_flush_guard disables flush if baseline eviction_rate > 200/s. long term we should instrument per-prefix throttling not global guard.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2983. Severity: P1. Owner: maria nguyen. Runbook: KV_CACHE_DEGRADATION -> continuous-batch rollback.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: alert acknowledged by maria nguyen at 11:12 UTC. Next on-call (carla reyes) will be handover in 2h.

leo park: after the batch_window revert, eviction_rate stabilized near baseline; paging_ops back within expected range; partial flush rates dropped to <1/min. trend graphs look steady for last 12m.

maria nguyen: good. please keep the continuous batching disabled until we validate a per-prefix admission control fix. @emily please keep incremental rollout paused at 60% until postmortem.

emily chen: pausing further rollouts. I'll open a PR for per-prefix token caps and a canary harness to exercise hot prefixes. link: https://git.redwood/infer/kv-cache/pulls/392

carla reyes: customer impact note: sending initial blurb to accounts for those tenants we saw error spikes on. Ops outreach queued.

maria nguyen: On-call handoff notes for @carla in 2h: what we changed, current metrics (eviction ~1.1x baseline, paging ops normal), mitigation steps taken, follow-ups (per-prefix caps PR, improved eviction alarms). Leaving a bridge channel for postmortem in #postmortems.

carla reyes: ACK. I'll take the handoff and keep monitoring. Will coordinate postmortem and ETA for per-prefix throttles.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-2983 status: mitigation applied, customer outreach started, monitoring for regressions. Next update in 30m or on-call handoff. :white_check_mark:
